newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef traded lower on good demand and heavy offerings, USDA said in its weekly carlot meat report for the week ended Thursday.

Good retail demand continued for both immediate and forward interest. Chuck and round cuts traded lower throughout the trading period as inventories on these cuts were quite a burden. Chuck cuts did manage to stabilize at the end of the week, but round cuts were still trading with a weak undertone.
Loin cuts also traded lower throughout the week and seemed to have started their seasonal decline a few weeks earlier than normal.
Rib cuts traded at steady levels early in the week, but by the middle of the week the Choice product encountered downward pressure.

The closely trimmed product followed the same pattern as the commodity and traded lower on good demand. Beef trimmings traded mostly steady early in the week, but reduced slaughter levels and improved demand at midweek helped stimulate beef trimmings higher the remainder of the trading period.

Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items traded lower on light to moderate demand and moderate offerings with the blended coarse ground items experiencing the biggest losses. A firm undertone was noted late in the week.

For the week Select and Choice rib primal steady to 3.00 lower; Select and Choice chuck primal 2.00 to 4.00 lower; Select and Choice round primal 2.00 to 2.50 lower; Select and Choice loin primal 6.00 lower; Closely trimmed item's 3.00 to 3.50 lower; Beef trimmings 1.00 higher; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items 2.00 to 6.00 lower.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 3.70 at 98.41; 700/850 Dn 3.03 at 98.16; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 2.86 at 92.78; 700/850 Dn 2.34 at 92.53.
